short.lead: You approved saving on every reply (1A), with me writing the handoff note (2A) and the note loading when a session opens on its branch (3A). This plan builds it in four steps, each its own issue under "Keep work saved and handed off on every reply, so a usage limit never strands it" (#406), which replaces #140. Step 3 fixes two bugs I found while planning, which affect every project thread like this one. Your standing rule says nothing reaches main with a known bug, so it is in this plan rather than left for later.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes and how it is proved.
items: Step 1 (#407): check that work is pushed and the handoff note is written

The end-of-reply check already sends a reply back once when files written this turn are uncommitted. It gains three more checks, run only when the turn wrote files or made a commit. First, the branch is pushed. Second, the handoff note docs/5-today/handoff-<branch>.md is not older than the newest commit. Third, the note carries no published page link, session link or Claude credit. A git command that fails is reported as "could not tell", never as a pass.
Step 2 (#408): the note loads at session start

When a session opens on a branch that has a note, the note's text is added to the session's context, with a first line naming the file. A long note is cut at a fixed size, and the loaded text says that it was cut.
Step 3 (#409): two approval bugs in project threads

In this thread, the stage file saved the feature as "usage limit handoff 1A 2A 3A</message>": the thread's message markup and your answer codes became part of the name. The second bug: your message "Design approved: background work tracking 1*" from another thread also moved this thread's stage, because it was passed to me as a quoted message. After the fix, quoted messages will not move the stage, and a feature name will end before any message markup or answer codes.
Step 4 (#410): tests, docs, version and a real run

Each step first adds test cases to verify.py (the script that checks the hooks do what the docs claim). The cases reproduce the fault or show the new behaviour, and then the code follows. The real run happens in a cloud session: a turn that edits a file and stops before pushing must be sent back, and a later session on the branch must load the note. The version is set at merge time, expected to be 2.75.0.
Approving moves the feature into Build, and I start on step 1.
